subjects.title: The standalone ovito Python distribution 3.15.5 is a distinct module execution surface with exact artifact, Python, platform, license, and imported-version requirements.
OVITO Basic desktop 3.15.5 is a separate MIT/open-source distribution surface and does not imply availability of the standalone Python module.
OVITO Pro desktop and ovitos 3.15.5 are proprietary entitlement-bound surfaces; installation metadata or an account does not establish authorization.
Python module, Basic desktop, Pro desktop, source documentation, third-party notices, user data, and generated artifacts have distinct identity and license boundaries.
ovito.io.import_file(location, **params) returns a Pipeline and has exact source, format, sequence, and sort_particles semantics.
Pipeline.compute(frame) evaluates a zero-based frame and returns an independent DataCollection snapshot.
FileSource.load replaces a pipeline source and must be recorded as an input-identity change.
ovito.io.export_file has frame, format, column, precision, identifier, and output-reparse semantics that must be explicit.
DataCollection, SimulationCell, particle properties, cell-vector column conventions, and frame metadata are version-bound API surfaces.
OVITO 3.15.5 XYZ/extxyz import has explicit property, coordinate, lattice, PBC, source-unit, frame, and parser mapping semantics.
Particle Identifier enables traceable cross-frame mapping; otherwise equal count and storage order remain assumptions, and sort_particles changes order.
Lattice, PBC, simulation-cell vectors, coordinate conventions, and source-native length units must be explicit before geometric analysis.
OVITO pipeline modifier order, selections, deletion, derived properties, and frame dependence affect results and must be recorded.
Coordination analysis and radial distribution functions require cutoff, pair/selection, PBC, normalization, binning, units, frame, and convergence evidence.
Common-neighbor analysis has version-bound mode, cutoff/adaptive behavior, structure labels, and validation limits.
Polyhedral template matching has template, RMSD, orientation, deformation, selection, and validation semantics.
Displacement vectors depend on reference configuration, cell deformation, mapping, PBC, affinity, and frame identity.
Atomic strain depends on reference mapping, cutoff/neighbors, cell deformation, least-squares conditioning, and output tensor conventions.
Wigner-Seitz defect analysis requires a validated reference lattice, mapping, occupancy interpretation, PBC, and cell compatibility.
Dislocation extraction analysis has crystal structure, circuit, line, Burgers-vector, smoothing, edition, and validation requirements.
Trajectory averaging requires explicit frame range, transient handling, property continuity, time weights, and uncertainty interpretation.
Rendering requires exact edition, renderer, camera, scene, colors, particle/box settings, fonts, codec, headless environment, frame range, and visual QA.
Export requires explicit object, format, frames, columns, precision, mapping, units, overwrite policy, and output reparse.
Images and animations are visual artifacts and cannot establish numerical defect, coordination, strain, topology, convergence, or physical correctness.
The exact v3.15.5 source repository declares OVITO user documentation under GFDL-1.2-or-later while software and third-party components have separate terms.
